source_stage_mapping.season_aggregation: features: preserve box-score ratios of summed totals with explicit possessions controls.
source_stage_mapping.graph_centralities: features: directed weighted loser-to-winner PageRank; no true strength-of-schedule certification.
source_stage_mapping.elo_ratings: features: chronological per-season Elo with explicit initialization, K and stable custom scale.
source_stage_mapping.pairwise_concatenation: pairings: A, B and A-B, mirrored fitting/calibration labels and both prediction orientations with strict chronology.
source_stage_mapping.logistic_regression: fit_scores, calibrate, forward, reverse, projection_inputs, sum, result: complete standardized logistic branch, separate held-out sigmoid, ordered orientation projection and lifecycle output.

limitations: Automated Tier 3 implementation qualification only; no human Tier 1 review or Tier 2 usage certification.
The source describes a generic benchmark topology, not an identified historical winning solution. No competitive accuracy or true strength-of-schedule claim is made.
Complete synthetic graph results match the unchanged reference. Matrix-only tests demonstrate mechanical reuse, not empirical cross-domain accuracy.

Season feature aggregation and mirrored chronological pairing retain the source recipe. Dense standardized binary fitting supports arbitrary positive feature widths; sigmoid fit/predict and ordered sum remain independently bound generic providers.
Intermediate provenance and population independence are caller responsibilities; shape and chronology checks do not authenticate them.
Existing sigmoid fitting does not check optimizer success. Finite calibration coefficients do not establish convergence; base logistic fitting does treat ConvergenceWarning as an error.
Installed package files match their own RECORD hashes; publisher authenticity, clean deployment, optional extras and other platforms remain unqualified.
Provider publication transaction gates and stored corrected-original CDG execution/publication remain separate requirements.
The original intake has only a generic benchmark description and Kaggle homepage citation; no historical winner or source-code parity is claimed.
The explicitly permitted logistic branch is fully implemented. XGBoost is an alternative branch, not an omitted mandatory stage.
PageRank remains a declared graph feature; the intake claim of true strength of schedule is unsupported and explicitly corrected.

Prediction rows are caller-enumerated. To evaluate every possible matchup, callers must provide all desired ordered pairs; the stored execution exercises all six pairs among three synthetic teams. The implementation does not infer tournament membership or silently add rows.

Current NumPy is 2.2.6 rather than historical 2.4.2. Current active requirements, actual imports, installed files and fresh full-reference comparisons pass; historical environment equivalence is not claimed.
Preparation validates only root fields, finite JSON and nonempty populations. Downstream stages enforce detailed numerical and chronological contracts.
Original history and derivative are preserved. Native publication, atomic activation and served selection remain separate gates.
